ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, a large square ABCD is composed of four congruent right-angled triangles and a small square. Points P and Q are the midpoints of AB and GH, respectively. If PQ happens to pass through point F, what is the value of $\frac{AB}{EF}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw line PM$\perp$BE at point M,\\
Let BE=a, GH=b,\\
since $\triangle AHD \cong \triangle BEA$,\\
therefore AH=BE=a,\\
since quadrilateral EFGH is a square,\\
therefore FG=GH=EH=EF=b,\\
since $\angle AEB = \angle PMB = 90^\circ$,\\
therefore PM$\parallel$AE,\\
therefore BP:AP=BM:ME,\\
since point P is the midpoint of AB,\\
therefore AP=BP,\\
therefore BM=EM=$\frac{1}{2}$a,\\
therefore PM is the median of $\triangle ABE$,\\
therefore PM=$\frac{1}{2}$AE=$\frac{1}{2}$(a−b),\\
furthermore, since point Q is the midpoint of GH,\\
therefore GQ=$\frac{1}{2}$GH=$\frac{1}{2}$b,\\
since $\angle PMF = \angle BFC = 90^\circ$,\\
therefore $\triangle PMF \sim \triangle FGQ$,\\
therefore PM:FG=MF:GQ,\\
therefore PM$\times$GQ=FG$\times$MF,\\
since MF=EM−EF=$\frac{1}{2}$a−b,\\
therefore $\frac{1}{2}$(a−b)$\times\frac{1}{2}$b=b($\frac{1}{2}$a−b),\\
Upon simplification, we get $3b^2−ab=0$, i.e., $b(3b−a)=0$,\\
since b$\neq$0,\\
therefore 3b−a=0,\\
therefore a=3b,\\
therefore AE=AH−EH=a−b=2b,\\
therefore $AB=\sqrt{AE^2+BE^2}=\sqrt{(2b)^2+(3b)^2}=\sqrt{13}b$,\\
therefore $AB:EF = \boxed{\sqrt{13}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a large square ABCD with A at the upper left, B at the lower left, C at the lower right, and D at the upper right. Point P lies on AB, point Q lies on GH, and the segment PQ passes through F. Reasoning: Let EF = EH = b and AE = x. Use coordinates with E = (0,0), the x-axis along EH, and the y-axis along EF. Then H = (b,0), F = (0,b), G = (b,b), and A = (-x,0). Since the four outer right triangles are congruent, BE = AH. Here AH = AE + EH = x + b, so BE = x + b. Because B, F, E are collinear, B = (0,x+b). P is the midpoint of AB, so P = ((-x+0)/2, (0+x+b)/2) = (-x/2, (x+b)/2). Q is the midpoint of GH, so Q = (b, b/2). Since P, F, Q are collinear, the vectors P - F and Q - F are parallel. Now P - F = (-x/2, (x-b)/2), and Q - F = (b, -b/2). Their determinant must be zero: (-x/2)(-b/2) - ((x-b)/2)b = 0. This gives xb/4 - b(x-b)/2 = 0, so x/4 - (x-b)/2 = 0, hence -x + 2b = 0, so x = 2b. Therefore AE = 2b and BE = x + b = 3b. Thus AB = sqrt(AE^2 + BE^2) = sqrt((2b)^2 + (3b)^2) = sqrt(13)b. Since EF = b, AB/EF = sqrt(13).
